ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA), as amended; Law of 12 November 2004 on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended (transposing EU AML Directives 4, 5 and 6); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulations of 25 January 2019 and 7 March 2019 relating to beneficial ownership registration; Luxembourg Criminal Code and sanctions implementation regulations under EU Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) decisions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport Copy of each Director, Authorised Signatory and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary, embassy or consular authority in the country of residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin; if the country of origin is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, full Consular Legalization through the nearest Luxembourg or other EU embassy is mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing, Certificate of Incorporation or Recent Corporate Extract of each direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent issuing authority of the country of origin, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorising the incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL and the appointment of local counsel/notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent corporate authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states), with certified translation into French by a Luxembourg sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Fully executed Luxembourg Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif de la S.à r.l.)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary admitted to the Chamber des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not applicable to foreign authentication; the original notarial deed is registered directly with the RCS/LBR and published in the RESA without consular legalisation or apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004 as amended: all UBOs, directors, signatories and direct shareholders must be screened against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2010 and related CFSP decisions), UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, HMT UK consolidated sanctions list, and the national lists of Luxembourg (FIU/CRF, Ministry of Finance, CSSF administrative sanctions); Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) identified per EU Directive 2015/849 and subsequent amendments, requiring senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and continuous monitoring. Screening must be repeated not less than every 30 days while the incorporation is pending and at least annually thereafter for the entire lifetime of the entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu and RESA publication portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The deed of incorporation, company name and statutory seat denomination must be drafted in French. A Luxembourg S.à r.l. must bear a name that is not identical or confusingly similar to names already registered in the RCS or protected under IP law, and the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or its recognised abbreviated form 'S.à r.l.' must be included. Foreign-character trade names are transliterated into the Latin script using French/Luxembourgish orthographic rules, and the RCS will refuse scripts such as Chinese, Cyrillic or Arabic characters in the statutory corporate name unless a registered transliteration is supplied, which then becomes the statutory name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANK / TRUST (requires prior authorisation from the Ministry of Finance and, if relevant, CSSF licence)
ASSURANCE / INSURANCE / RÉASSURANCE (requires prior authorisation from the Commissariat aux Assurances)
FONDS D'INVESTISSEMENT / INVESTMENT FUND / SUB-FUND (requires CSSF approval and Part II/Part I fund law registration)
AUDIT / RÉVISEUR D'ENTREPRISES (requires Institut Luxembourgeois des Administrateurs Certificate or profession authorisation)
ETAT / NATIONAL / OFFICIEL / ADMINISTRATION (implies state affiliation and is prohibited absent ministerial consent)
BOURSE / STOCK EXCHANGE / CLEARING (requires financial-market regulator authorisation)
CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE / FÉDÉRATION PROFESSIONNELLE (reserved to actual professional associations)
FIDUCIAIRE / FIDUCIARY / NOMINEE (requires specific Ministry of Justice professional approval under the Law of 12 November 2004)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg law does not provide a statutory name-reservation register separate from the RCS; the notary carries out a de facto pre-clearance check in LBR/RESA and holds the chosen name for up to 30 days pending execution of the notarial deed. If the RCS Registrar refuses the requested name at registration, the notary immediately files a corrective deed or an amended name request identifying a new distinguishing token in the LBR electronic portal. If the Registrar confirms an official refusal, an administrative appeal must be addressed to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, Civil Commercial Chamber) within one month of the written refusal, pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and RESA, as amended; the notary and local counsel will attach a notarised copy of the deed, a conflict report evidencing availability of alternative names, and written submissions showing absence of confusion. Interim injunctive proceedings can be brought where the refusal causes imminent financial harm. The legal cost of such an appeal ranges from EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 in counsel fees plus court registration duties.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office with no verifiable physical street address is not permissible for a Luxembourg S.à r.l. Professional domiciliation by an approved domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation) is accepted where the agent is licensed under the Law of 12 November 2004 and the Law of 1 August 2001 on the exercise of certain financial professions; the registered office must be a genuine, identifiable address within Luxembourg where the RCS, tax authorities and notaries can serve legal process. For a MarTech/SaaS analytics tool using Stripe and Paddle payment rails, a domiciliation address is commercially accepted, but the entity must nonetheless retain local operational substance, at least through a local authorised administrator, accounting records, and directors with appropriate management capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for ISIC 6201 low-risk standard AML tier: quantified annualised probability of an unannounced on-site physical inspection is estimated below 5%. However, if suspicious transactions, missing annual filings, or mismatch between declared activity and actual digital footprint are detected, the RCS, Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes – ACD), and the FIU/Cellule de Renseignements Financiers (CRF) may perform unannounced inspections on very short notice. The registered office must demonstrate commercial substance on demand, including staff presence, server/cloud administration support, accounting documentation and management oversight, within 24 hours.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) for a S.à r.l., including statutory name clearance verification and drafting of the articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg; fee collected by the drafting notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff under Grand-Ducal regulation, based on share capital brackets and statutory ancillary operations; EUR 1,500–2,200 market benchmark for a standard SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic filing of the incorporation file and registrations in the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) and the LBR electronic portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS/LBR administrative registration levy, as revised by the Law of 19 December 2002 and LBR fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed and statutory particulars in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA) through the RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic publication handled by the RCS; no significant separate tariff beyond the RCS filing fee; EUR 0–50 market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration and beneficial-ownership registration with the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), including the identification documents of all 25% UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) through the Ministry of Justice / LBR platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-filing administrative fee on the LBR/RBE; short schedules additional per UBO or director

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalisation of foreign corporate and passport documents issued in connection with the incorporation bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO, Hong Kong Apostille Service, Chinese foreign affairs office or relevant notary office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention or consular legalisation fee; USD 25–60 per certified document, assuming two to three bundled documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation of foreign apostilled or legalised documents (articles, passports, powers of attorney and certificates of good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator authorised by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice or the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark of EUR 45–90 per translated page for certified legal translations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC identity verification, PEP and sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories against EU/UN/OFAC/HMT and Luxembourg CRF lists
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary as AML obliged entity, assisted by external compliance/software provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: AML professional fee benchmark; EUR 80–180 depending on the number of screened individuals and continuous monitoring frequency

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and professional domiciliation service for the first year at a regulated provider in Luxembourg City / Kirchberg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorised domiciliation agent under the Law of 12 November 2004 and Law of 1 August 2001
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for commercial domiciliation of a low-risk SaaS company; EUR 800–1,200 per annum excluding ancillary mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly or fixed-fee market benchmark of EUR 1,200–2,500 for coordinated incorporation workflow of a foreign-owned SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial ancillary fee schedule for copies and certificates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; SARL provisions under Articles 104 et seq.; registration provisions under Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) rules and the Law of 14 August 2000 on trade and company registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); notaries act as mandatory e-filers for incorporation acts.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and articles of association (statuts), lodged with the RCS by the notary; mandatory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 statutory minimum for a Luxembourg SARL; the entire capital must be fully subscribed and paid up in cash before notarization; funds are held in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution and are released only upon RCS registration. A special auditor's report is required only for non-cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, by the sole shareholder of [●] Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), effective upon incorporation:

1. The entire issued share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 1,200 registered shares of EUR 10 each, fully subscribed and paid in, is approved.

2. The registered office is fixed at [●], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; the manager is authorized to change it as provided by law.

3. [●] is appointed Gérant (manager) for an indefinite term, with sole signature authority and all powers to operate the business, including opening bank accounts and executing SaaS agreements.

4. The Gérant is authorized to complete all RCS, RES, tax, VAT, and social security registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-file portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request through the LBR e-file system or instruct the notary to verify availability in the RCS database. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must comply with public-order and misleading-name prohibitions, and must contain the mandatory legal-form suffix 'S.à r.l.'.
required_dossiers: proposed company name and legal form
draft articles of association
passport copies of shareholders and intended manager
LuxTrust certificate for electronic authentication
summary of corporate purpose and object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, submit a revised name with a distinctive element, obtain a statement of no objection, or file an administrative challenge before the Luxembourg administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Escrow and Initial Bank Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved Luxembourg credit institution or notary's dedicated client escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit at least EUR 12,000 as fully paid-up share capital. Instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate (attestation de libération) addressed to the notary, confirming that the funds shall not be released to the company until the RCS registration is completed.
required_dossiers: bank account opening application
draft articles of association
AML/KYC identification of all shareholders
ultimate beneficial owner declaration
source-of-funds statement or supporting transfer records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional AML or economic-substance documentation, provide the full transaction chain and notarized shareholder declarations, then obtain a corrected blocking certificate for the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The shareholders execute the notarial deed of incorporation and the articles of association before a Luxembourg notary. The notary verifies legal capacity, the paid-in capital certificate, corporate purpose, registered office, and the appointment of the Gérant. The deed is drawn up in French or German, with an English translation if desired, and the notary prepares the RCS filing package.
required_dossiers: draft statutes and incorporation deed
bank attestation of paid-in and blocked capital
passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
ultimate beneficial owner register form
lease agreement or landowner consent for registered office
written acceptance of appointment by the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects missing statutory clauses or irregular signatures, prepare a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) or a supplementary notarial minute and re-execute the deed before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Legal Publication in RES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Central RCS filing office through mandatory notary e-filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the executed incorporation deed, statutes, and supporting annexes to the LBR through the authorized e-filing channel. The LBR verifies compliance, allocates the Luxembourg trade register number (numéro RCS), and arranges publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés. Upon completion, the company obtains its legal existence and extracts evidencing the registered office and manager appointments.
required_dossiers: notarial incorporation deed and articles of association
bank release/blocking certificate and proof of capital payment
RCS filing declaration generated by the notary
proof of payment of the official RCS filing fee
publication sheet for Recueil électronique des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an observation or requests further particulars, the notary files a rectification deed; if publication is materially incomplete, the company obtains a corrected excerpt from LBR and requests re-publication in the RES.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security, and Office Occupancy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); local municipal authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the post-incorporation regulatory filings: register for Luxembourg VAT and corporate income tax through the relevant registration forms on MyGuichet or via the appointed accountant; register as an employer with CCSS for social security; file the office-occupancy declaration with the local commune; obtain fire-safety clearance for the leased premises; and ensure ITM workplace compliance. For a pure software analytics SaaS business, no industrial establishment permit or environmental operating licence is required.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and extract
VAT registration application and income tax registration form
lease agreement and floor plan of registered office
passport and professional details of the Gérant
social security employer registration form
fire-safety and electrical conformity declarations for office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commune or ITM raises premises-compliance objections, submit amended floor plans, lease amendments, or remedial fire-safety works; if the VAT or social-security classification is disputed, file an administrative appeal with the AEDT or CCSS within the applicable one-month statutory window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry, Innovation and Research (not applicable for ISIC 6201 software analytics; no industrial establishment permit required)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required for a non-regulated MarTech/SaaS software analytics activity under Luxembourg professional-access rules; only RCS registration and ordinary office occupancy clearance apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environment Agency) of the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no environmental impact assessment or category rating triggered for an office-based software analytics tool; classed as non-industrial administrative occupation under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable industrial wastewater, VOC, or point-source emission thresholds; compliance required for office waste management (municipal certified collection), WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU for electronic equipment, and minimum energy-performance standards for commercial premises

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: registered office must secure a municipal fire-safety certificate for commercial occupancy, including emergency exits, extinguishers, and electrical installation conformity. Occupational: ITM workstation compliance under the Luxembourg Labour Code, including ergonomic equipment, electrical safety, and office ventilation; structural load inspections are not required for standard software-office use. No special civil-defense authorization is needed for a non-industrial office workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Inland Revenue) — impotsdirects.public.lu. Indirect taxes: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — pfi.public.lu. Unified e-filing and business portal: myguichet.lu / guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL is incorporated through the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), which immediately grants the statutory 13-digit matricule (national tax ID) used for direct-tax, social security and statistical filings. Upon completion of incorporation registration, the AEDT automatically assigns the VAT identification number in the format LU 0000 0000 where the company carries on taxable activities; where automatic assignment does not occur, the SARL must file VAT registration Form 100 (resident) via myguichet.lu. A foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment does not obtain a LU VAT ID for pure B2C e-service traffic: it uses the non-Union OSS (third-country supplies) or Union OSS (intra-EU supplies). A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg permanent establishment registers via Form 100A and must appoint a VAT representative in Luxembourg only if it has no EU establishment and would otherwise become liable for import VAT or direct registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SARL is a resident company (LIR section 159: registered office and central administration in Luxembourg) taxed on worldwide income, with no pass-through eligibility. The complete charge comprises corporate income tax (17% headline), unemployment fund surcharge (7% on CIT) and municipal business tax; combined statutory headline approximately 24.94% in Luxembourg City (rates vary by municipality), plus net wealth tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-transparent election is available; the SARL is per se opaque. Applicable statutory elections: (i) fiscal unity / tax consolidation under LIR section 164ter (95% direct or indirect shareholding held for at least one uninterrupted fiscal year, covering CIT and municipal business tax); (ii) VAT group assessment (solidarité) under Article 52 of the VAT law, allowing the SARL and its Luxembourg sub-entities to file under one VAT number; (iii) Union OSS / IOSS election for intra-EU B2C e-services and distance sales, displacing Luxembourg place-of-supply rules; (iv) participation exemption (LIR section 166) applying automatically to qualifying substantial holdings, with a formal declaration option for the capital-gains limb; (v) binding tax rulings for advanced confirmation of hybrid financing structures; and (vi) ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules apply mandatorily, with grandfathering elections only for pre-2016 structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) governed by the amended law of 12 February 1979 and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established businesses (raised from EUR 30,000 effective 1 January 2023); EUR 10,000 calendar-year threshold for intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C electronically-supplied services below which Luxembourg VAT applies locally and above which destination-state VAT applies via Union OSS; no registration threshold for foreign suppliers established outside Luxembourg (registration from the first euro of taxable supplies unless the non-Union OSS is used).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government digital stamping, or SDI-style approval system applies to B2B/B2C invoicing. Mandatory PEPPOL-based e-invoicing applies only to B2G supplies (EN 16931/UBL) since 1 January 2021. B2B e-invoices are optional but must guarantee authenticity, integrity and legibility (EDI or qualified electronic signature). VAT returns are filed monthly or quarterly via myguichet.lu (deadline: 15th of the month following the period), EC sales lists are filed monthly/quarterly per value thresholds, and OSS returns are filed quarterly via the EU OSS portal. Records must be retained for 10 years; no digital stamp or clearance code is issued by the AEDT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to export supplies to non-EU destinations and intra-Community supplies within the EU when the goods leave Luxembourg under transport evidence; export must be evidenced within 90 days from the time of supply (Implementing Regulation 282/2011). Digital SaaS services (SEO crawler and keyword analytics tool): supplies to non-EU business and private customers are outside Luxembourg VAT scope because the place of supply is the customer's establishment or residence (no Luxembourg output VAT and no refund claim needed); supplies to EU business customers are reverse-charged at the customer's member state upon presentation of a valid EU VAT ID; supplies to EU consumers are VAT-liable in the consumer's state and reported through Union OSS once the EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold is met. The exporter must satisfy the invoice-content requirements of Articles 57-61 of the Luxembourg VAT law and hold commercial evidence proving the foreign destination and the customer's non-EU status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/DAU) endorsed by the customs office of exit from the EU
Transport document: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR/road consignment note evidencing physical departure
Commercial invoice containing the Luxembourg VAT ID and express mention of the zero-rate or outside-scope treatment
Evidence of the customer's non-EU establishment (valid foreign VAT/tax ID or, for B2C, payment-leg data and geolocation/IP evidence)
Executed SaaS licence or service contract and customer acceptance certificate
FX inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement proving receipt of the foreign currency proceeds from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may, on audit, require the complete zero-rating/outside-scope evidence file. Missing, forged or contradictory export or FX documentation retroactively destroys the zero-rating, resulting in reassessment of 17% Luxembourg VAT, default interest, and administrative fines under Article 66 of the VAT law (per-offence fines) and criminal prosecution under Article 69 (imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and/or substantial criminal fines) where fraudulent intent is demonstrated. The assessment/recovery window is generally three years from the end of the year in which the tax became chargeable and is extended to ten years in cases of fraud or intentional concealment. Company directors are jointly liable for the reinstated VAT, interest and penalties, and repeat offenders may face a public blacklisting effect within the AEDT enforcement file.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in cooperation with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a founding member of the Eurozone and fully applies the free movement of capital under TFEU Article 63. No distinction exists between current-account and capital-account convertibility; both are unrestricted. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred without exchange-control approval. Subject only to standard tax formalities and AML verification, no prior or post-transaction FX authorizations are required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirements in Luxembourg. Enterprises may retain export revenues in the currency of receipt and may continue to hold any freely convertible currency without prior authorization. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL applies above material thresholds, with strict data confidentiality.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High. Luxembourg recognizes Electronic Money Institution (EMI) and Payment Institution (PI) status, governed by the CSSF under PSD2. An offshore digital EMI can offer virtual IBANs and facilitate cross-border collection from Stripe/Paddle, but it cannot provide core deposit-account services and must not hold client funds as bank deposits. For a low-risk SaaS analytics tool, an online EMI is a viable ancillary collection rail, yet the capital escrow account and primary operating liquidity must remain with a Tier-1 Luxembourg commercial bank to satisfy statutory public-deposit and substance expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted under CSSF AML/KYC circulars for low-risk legal entities; identity verification may be completed via video conference and electronic signature. However, most Luxembourg Tier-1 banks retain a de facto policy requiring at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person interview at the bank's head office when opening the corporate account, with the dossiers and signatories present. An alternative is a notarized power of attorney held by a locally admitted corporate service provider, but the bank retains the final discretion to demand physical appearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity is newly incorporated, has no operating history, and no audited financial statements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Initial share capital deposit certificate, bank reference from the founding shareholder's bank, detailed business plan with project costs, revenue forecast from the SEO tool subscriptions, and frameworks for future VAT and profit tax registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is not physically present in Luxembourg or the EEA.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration, certified passport copies, corporate chart from the shareholder to the natural person, signed AML/KYC questionnaire, and evidence of the UBO's professional track record in software/SaaS businesses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border inflows from high-friction jurisdictions or third-party payment processors (Stripe/Paddle).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial SaaS agreements with clients, copies of payment processor onboarding confirmations, source-of-funds declarations, and a forecast of transaction volumes with geographic breakdown and end-customer legitimacy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low substance indicators: no physical office, no employees in Luxembourg, no payroll history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rent agreement for registered office, status of local payroll or outsourced HR provider, planned hiring roadmap, VAT registration, and a tangible operational substance dossier demonstrating decision-making, IT infrastructure, and server utilization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-off capital injection requirement for development of the SEO analytics platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution approving the capital injection, bank statements evidencing the source of funds, notarized shareholders' agreement, proof of the SaaS product roadmap, and auditable cap-table analysis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder wiring must be directed to the designated share capital escrow account at a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. The SWIFT transfer must clearly reference the shareholder corporate name and use the purpose code 'Capital contribution / Share issuance' (purpose code GR005 under EU statistical standards). Third-party payments are strictly prohibited. When the shareholder is resident outside the EEA, the bank requires a resolution approving the capital increase, notarized subscription deeds, and evidence of the funding source. For USD-denominated injections, the bank executes a spot conversion; for repeated USD funding, a EUR/USD forward can be pre-arranged.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a low-risk MarTech SaaS entity with no physical goods, the primary outbound rails are SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments, SWIFT MT103 for USD and all non-EUR currencies, and SWIFT GPI for instant and traceable priority settlements. Recurring license or software procurement payments are executed via standard MT103 with 'SHA' charges and the advantageous correspondent-bank route (e.g., EUR via TARGET2/ECMS, USD via BNY Mellon or BNP's New York branch). A documentary Commercial Letter of Credit may be used for large bespoke hardware or infrastructure procurement, though it is not needed for recurring subscription-based disbursements. For intra-EU suppliers, the SEPA Direct Debit B2B scheme is permitted for invoiced amounts, while cross-border vendor payments should be settled only via MT103 to avoid unnecessary deductions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD forward outrights (offered by all Luxembourg Tier-1 banks under ISDA or local master agreements; must be booked through the corporate treasury account).
EUR/USD FX swaps (used for short-term liquidity and margin management without EPU exposure).
EUR/USD currency options (covered over-the-counter with CSSF reporting; requires an investment approval board resolution).
ISDA-form long-term currency swaps (suitable for EUR/USD interest-rate and principal conversion on shareholder loans or vendor financing).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are prohibited for EUR/USD because the euro is fully convertible; NDF instruments are permissible only for exotic non-convertible remuneration currencies and then require BCL statistical reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (financial statements and annual report) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS formal reminder and court order risk; late deposit is sanctioned by a Luxembourg court fine (up to EUR 125,000) and persistent default can lead to judicial winding-up or administrative striking-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 31 December of the calendar year following the taxable fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the standard return must be filed by 31 December of the following year, subject to extension on justified request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers ex officio assessment, default interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid tax, administrative penalties up to 10% of additional tax, and possible criminal prosecution for deliberate concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of the beneficial owners declaration (RBE / UBO register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every calendar year; within one (1) month of any change in beneficial ownership or direct/indirect control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default is a criminal offence: individual directors/managers may be fined up to EUR 1,250,000 (or imprisoned for up to five years) depending on gravity; corporate fines also apply to the SARL.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds in each of two consecutive financial years: (i) balance-sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; (ii) net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; (iii) average workforce above 50 employees. Public-interest entities and listed companies must always appoint an approved statutory auditor ('réviseur d'entreprises agréé').
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts of undertakings (as amended, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); simplified formats for micro/small entities are available; IFRS as adopted by the EU is used by listed/consolidated groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the SARL must verify that the RBE/UBO filing remains accurate and confirm/update it through the LBR online portal. Beneficial ownership disclosure applies to any natural person who holds or controls, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the shares/voting rights or who otherwise exercises control. Any share transfer or change in qualifying control must be entered in the partners' register and disclosed to the RBE within one month; the company's managers remain personally responsible for timely filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shares and Transfer Records
Minute Book of shareholders' and managers' resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 12,000 per year (mandatory only above audit thresholds; not required for small SARL)

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Modele 200) - annual corporation tax return combining corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; filed via MyGuichet.lu using LUXTRUST/ eID authentication (paper only on express ACD approval).
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual (tax year equals the accounting year; calendar-year accounting is statutory default unless the articles provide otherwise).
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: For a year ending 31 December N, the return is due by 31 December N+1 as set by ACD circular; a company may apply in writing for additional extension (usually granted for audit not yet completed). Non-resident companies with Luxembourg source income use the same deadline.
